lesson.title: Beat and Time Signatures
lesson.summary: Beats fall into regular groups; the time signature tells how many beats a bar has and how each beat divides.

section.title: Beat and bar
section.p: The beat is the steady pulse you tap your foot to. In most music some beats feel stronger than others, and the strong beats return regularly: every second, third or fourth beat.

Bar lines divide the music into bars of equal length, each starting with a strong beat, the downbeat. American English calls a bar a measure. A double bar line marks the end of a section, and a final bar line, thin and thick, the end of the piece.

figure.staff: *E4/q G4/q C5/q B4/q | *A4/h G4/h | *F4/q A4/q G4/q D4/q | *C4/w |.
figure.caption: Four bars of four beats. The downbeat of every bar is highlighted.

section.p: The grouping of beats is called the meter: two beats to a bar is duple meter, three is triple meter and four is quadruple meter.

check.prompt: The strong beat returns on every third beat. What is the meter?
check.explanation: Each bar starts with a strong beat, so a strong beat on every third beat means three beats to a bar: triple meter.

section.title: Simple time signatures
section.p: The time signature at the start of the music shows the meter with two numbers. Some American textbooks call it the meter signature. In simple time, the two numbers mean:

list.li: The top number: how many beats there are in a bar.
The bottom number: which note value gets one beat. 2 means a half note, 4 a quarter note and 8 an eighth note.

section.p: So 3/4 has three quarter-note beats in a bar, 2/4 two, and 4/4 four. In 2/2 the beat is a half note.

figure.staff: G4/h B4/q | D5/q C5/q B4/q | A4/h. |.
figure.caption: Triple meter in 3/4: strong, weak, weak.

section.p: In duple meter the beats go strong, weak. In triple meter they go strong, weak, weak. In quadruple meter the third beat is a little stronger than the second and fourth: strong, weak, medium, weak.
Two signs replace numbers. Common time, a sign shaped like a large C, means 4/4. The same sign with a vertical stroke through it is cut time, or alla breve, and means 2/2.
A bar in which nothing is played is written with a whole rest, even when the bar is shorter than a whole note.

figure.caption: In 3/4, the silent middle bar has a whole rest in the middle of the bar.

check.prompt: What does the bottom number of the time signature 3/2 tell you?
check.option: That a half note gets one beat
That there are two beats in a bar
That every beat divides into two
check.explanation: The top number counts the beats and the bottom number names the note value of one beat: 2 stands for a half note. 3/2 has three half-note beats in a bar.

check.prompt: Which time signature fits these two bars?

figure.description: Two bars without a time signature. The first has a half note and a quarter note; the second has three quarter notes.

check.explanation: A half note and a quarter note make three quarter-note beats, and so do three quarter notes: each bar has three quarter-note beats, which is 3/4.

section.title: Compound time
section.p: In simple time each beat divides into two equal parts. In compound time each beat divides into three. The beat is then a dotted note: a dotted quarter note divides into three eighth notes.
Compound time signatures have 6, 9 or 12 as the top number. They count the divisions, not the beats: 6/8 has six eighth notes in a bar, grouped as two dotted-quarter beats.

figure.staff: C5/e D5/e E5/e F5/e E5/e D5/e | C5/q. G4/q. |.
figure.caption: 6/8: two beats in a bar, each divided into three eighth notes.

section.p: 3/4 and 6/8 both hold six eighth notes in a bar, but they are grouped differently. 3/4 has three beats of two eighth notes; 6/8 has two beats of three. The beams show the difference.

figure.staff: E5/e D5/e C5/e D5/e E5/e C5/e | D5/h. |.
figure.caption: In 3/4, six eighth notes are beamed in three pairs: three beats, each divided into two.

figure.staff: E5/e D5/e C5/e D5/e E5/e C5/e | D5/h. |.
figure.caption: In 6/8, the same six eighth notes are beamed in two groups of three: two beats, each divided into three.

step.p: Look at the top number. 9 can be divided by three and is larger than three, so the meter is compound.
Divide the top number by three to get the number of beats: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 beats in a bar.
Each beat is three of the bottom number's value: three eighth notes, which is a dotted quarter note. 9/8 is compound triple meter with three dotted-quarter beats.

figure.staff: G4/e A4/e B4/e C5/e B4/e A4/e G4/q. |.

callout.p: Top number 2, 3 or 4: simple time, and the top number counts the beats. Top number 6, 9 or 12: compound time, and the top number divided by three counts the beats.

check.prompt: At a moderate tempo, how many beats does a bar of 6/8 have?
check.explanation: 6/8 is compound duple: six eighth notes grouped in two dotted-quarter beats. Only at a very slow tempo do performers count all six eighth notes.

check.prompt: How is the meter of 12/8 described?
check.explanation: 12 divided by three gives four dotted-quarter beats, each divided into three eighth notes: compound quadruple.

section.title: The upbeat
section.p: Music does not always begin on a downbeat. Notes before the first full bar form an upbeat, also called an anacrusis or a pickup. They lead into the first downbeat.
The upbeat is counted as the end of an incomplete bar. Often the last bar of the piece is shortened by the same amount, so that the first and last bars together make one full bar.

figure.staff: E4/q | *A4/h B4/q | C5/q B4/q A4/q | E5/h D5/q | C5/h |.
figure.caption: A one-beat upbeat in 3/4 leads into the downbeat; the last bar has the two remaining beats.

check.prompt: A piece in 4/4 starts with one quarter note before the first bar line. What is this note called?
check.explanation: Notes before the first full bar are an upbeat, or anacrusis. The downbeat is the first beat of a full bar, which comes right after it.
